utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. May I remind you of the affirmation you took at the beginning of your evidence, which still applies: There was an objection to evidence yesterday concerning one mortar. It has been decided in the exercise of discretion to allow that evidence. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Pepic.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Towards the end of the day yesterday, you mentioned some firing positions of the Croatian side that you saw in the Old Town of Dubrovnik, and I should now like to ask you to take a look at this map carefully and to mark the spot where it was that you saw this from Zarkovica, where you were that morning. So could you please place that on the overhead projector and place a cross at the spot at which you saw the artillery pieces of the Croatian side, and next to each of these pieces please write a number. And then we'll go on to explain what you saw and what all this was about. But carefully and slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to turn the map in my own line of vision, the way I saw the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Please put the map in front of you, and once you have marked it, place it back on the ELMO. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be a good idea if I had a magic marker.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I can't see where you've put the cross.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can the witness be provided with a magic marker, please, because we can't see the pencil mark.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the position of the mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Pepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is there a magic marker in the house in some colour so we can make a visible cross and marking on the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you use the magic marker now, please.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, unless I'm mistaken, you mentioned having seen flashes from one of the lateral streets on Stradun, towards Stradun. Did you mark that on the map?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I thought you just meant the entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Now, next to each of these spots, points, could you add a number, please.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pepic, what have you marked with number 1? What did you see there and where is it? Where's the location, the spot, number 1?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 1 is the mortar, the mortar that was moved. It was pulled out and withdrawn into a shelter. Now, whether it entered town or not, I wasn't able to see that. Number 2 --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Just slowly, please. So that was number 1.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you see that piece fire, the number 1 piece?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not, because my attention wasn't geared towards it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, number 2, what is that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 2 is an anti-aircraft gun, 20-millimetre. As far as I could see, it was up at Kula and firing from Kula. I didn't see it actually fire. I was told that it fired by my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, number 3, what is that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 3 is the observed fire, the flashes that came from the side-streets. I'm not sure whether it was this street or that street. That is why I marked the two spots. But it was one artillery piece, not two pieces, just one. And it was in the centre, to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You say you saw flashes. What kind of flashes were they?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were flashes when you fire a mortar shell. The firing of a mortar shell. You get these flashes of light.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How were you able to recognise that these were flashes of light when a shell, a mortar shell, or any other shell, is fired?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was my assumption, and I based and confirmed my assumption by the testimony of other commanding officers. The shells were falling all over Bosanka and Strincjera, coming from that spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you sign the map, and I'd like to tender the map into evidence as a Defence exhibit. And put today's date as well, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I tender this map as a Defence exhibit, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document is marked D104.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pepic, did you on that day, that is to say the 6th of December, see firing at JNA units from some positions that were not in the Old Town but were in the vicinity or near the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, what you observed and from what point, from where.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said yesterday, this was from the tennis courts by the Libertas Hotel, and it is the line of vision, Zarkovica, Stari Grad, Babin Kuk, that line of vision.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you notice any firing in the area between the Old Town on the slopes of Srdj? And if you did, please tell us. If not, we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the slopes of Mount Srdj, I noticed -- no, I did not notice them firing -- any firing from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: From Zarkovica, was there firing on these fire positions that you marked on the map that was in front of you a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Was there firing, to the best of your knowledge, exclusively targeting the fire-power positions of the opposite side?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The firing came exclusively from --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... the counsel is testifying.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel, please. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Counsel is testifying. These are very important areas and the witness should be testifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You are very clearly putting the answers you want to the witness, and this is a very important area. Now watch the questioning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: At what targets were fired at from Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I started to say, the firing came from targets, fire targets, from a number of directions, whether from Strincjera or the slopes of Srdj, and the firing came, what I saw, the firing came from the Maljutka laser type weapon, the 9K11. It was targeting the mortar, the anti-cannon gun to the right and the mortar to the left, and the mortar that I saw firing in the -- on the left-hand side -- on the left street of Stradun.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Who ordered the opening of fire, the firing that you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know about the chain of command, but the command of the anti-armoured company gave the order, and I suppose his superior Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. commander gave him the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And who was the superior commander?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Captain Kovacevic, the battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, who fired using the 9K11 Maljutka rocket?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the platoon did, of the launching pieces. He was an active duty-officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure. I think his name was Hodza. At least that's what they called him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did anybody else open fire from the Maljutka 9K11s on that morning on the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, Captain Nesic, company commander, fired from a mortar, and I later learnt, or rather, he told me that he had fired a number of rockets, but I didn't actually see that. So that means --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I be allowed to finish, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Captain Nesic used the mortar and fired --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Two grounds. He seemed to have finished his statement. And number 2, there is nothing, there is no disclosure to us that any discussion of Maljutkas was going to occur. In fact, yesterday, the Court said to counsel: Are you moving on to other areas? Are we finished with at least those items that we had already talked about? And counsel indicated he was. We're now beyond any type of disclosure. I have no objection to him testifying to these areas, but give the Prosecution some notice. This isn't trial by ambush.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, has there been notice about firing of Maljutkas?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we informed about the opening of fire, and we all know in this courtroom, very well, what was used to fire from Zarkovica. That was mentioned many times, and the Prosecution witness talked about that. So if we're talking about Zarkovica, in the presence of somebody at Zarkovica on that particular morning, of course we're going to mention everything that was testified to by Witness B, Witness Jokic. That goes without saying. And they did make mention of firing, the opening of fire. So I really don't see what additional information I ought to supply. And firing from Zarkovica was something that was included in the information and indeed during yesterday's testimony of this witness. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I take it from that that you accept that no notice was given of firing of Maljutkas.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Specifically about the Maljutka pieces, no. But about firing from Zarkovica, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would take the view, Mr. Petrovic, that you should not ask further questions about the Maljutka.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, of course I have to abide by your ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pepic, let us not mention the Maljutkas any more. So we're just discussing the firing, the opening of fire from Zarkovica. Was there any competition in opening fire from Zarkovica on that morning of the 6th of December, for example, 1991?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Heaven forbid. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could anybody who wanted to fire open fire on that morning from Zarkovica, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I be allowed to expand on this answer? At that point in time, there were at least three men dead by that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Answer only the questions that are put to you by counsel. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was impossible. We were busy saving lives. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What about warship Captain Zec? Was he present when fire was being opened from Zarkovica at those targets that you marked for us on the map that you have in front of you?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: My name is Philip Weiner. I work for the Office of the Prosecutor. I'm going to be asking you some questions, all right.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, have you ever been to the Old Town previously?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you're familiar with the area, of the Old Town, having been there several times?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you are aware its historical, cultural, and religious importance of the buildings that were in there? That were buildings of --

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that you know that within those walls of the Old Town, there are many very old buildings, practically ancient buildings?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you're aware that there were several religious buildings, churches, a synagogue, an Orthodox church, a mosque?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said before, I am aware of all these, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that you're aware that although the Stradun is a wide street or a large street, that there are many very small and narrow streets off the Stradun?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The side-streets. Stradun is the broadest street.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And some of those streets are so narrow you could practically put your hands on each side and touch the houses on each side, some of those streets are so narrow?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's typical of the way streets are built in Dalmatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you also know that there are tall buildings which they call palaces or we call town houses in the United States, and these tall buildings, you referred to a few of them on one of those side-streets, would you say they're roughly 16 to 18 metres tall?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They have many floors. I'm not sure about the height of those buildings, but if that's what you say, then you must be right, I guess. They are quite tall.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: They are quite tall. And you know it's a compact and congested area? You know that, sir? The Old Town, all those streets there, it's a compact and congested area within the walls?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Old Town, and it has ramparts around it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. Walls and ramparts. And you also know that there were people living there. Whether refugees or the locals, there were a lot of people living there in December 1991?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was not exactly a residential area of Dubrovnik, but there were quite a number of people living there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And people were living in those homes along those narrow streets in those palaces or town houses?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a lot of cafes there, but there were people living there too on the upper floors.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. And were you aware that the Old Town was a protected site, a UNESCO protected site?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By all means, yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you aware, as an observer, that there were orders that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the Old Town is not to be shelled?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. But no one was allowed to fire from it either.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware -- first, do you know who General Blagoje Adzic was at the time, the Chief of Staff for the Main Staff in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you aware of his orders not to shell cultural and protected property, that certain steps had to be taken before cultural and protected property was shelled?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even before he issued that order, we had already had clear orders not to shell any residential areas, or to avoid that as much as we could. But as soon as fire is opened from there, it becomes a target itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May the witness be shown Exhibit P119, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you go to the last page, the third page in the B/C/S, or the last page in the Bosnian/Serb/Croatian translation, which would be the last page in the English. The last sentence right above the signature. It says: It begins: I strictly -- do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And it says: "I strictly forbid the attacks on Dubrovnik." Correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: There is no qualifier there that you can fire upon Dubrovnik, even if you're receiving fire, is there, in that document?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the theory of war, this is not prescribed, but in theory, if we're suffering casualties from somewhere, we have to spot the place clearly and we have to define it as a firing position, which must be targeted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you about this order from the commander of the 2nd Operational Group, dated 24 October 1991, and it says: "I strictly forbid the attacks in Dubrovnik." It doesn't indicate any qualifier, saying that you can fire under certain conditions. This letter right here. This order right here. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown D47, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that again is from your commander, the commander of the 2nd Operational Group. And if you look at paragraph 4 -- could you look at that, please.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And it says: "Do not open fire at the Old Town in Dubrovnik." And there is a qualifier: "The units which are exposed to enemy fire are to be retreated to cover." Isn't that what it says?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And it says --

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Point 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: -- enemy fire troops are to retreat, the units are retreat. It doesn't have a qualifier saying if there's fire from the Old Town, you can return fire. It doesn't say that in that order to you, does it, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you know, as a soldier, and you're still a soldier to this day, you have to follow orders from your commanders?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, just to clarify the record; one of the lines isn't clear. In this letter I just showed you, this order I just showed you, there is no qualifier saying that you can fire upon the Old Town if they're firing outside -- if they're firing from the Old Town. There is nothing in this letter; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And finally, could the witness be shown, please, P16 -- P116. I'm sorry. P116.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, looking at this document, you can see that it's an order from the chief of the General Staff. And could you go to paragraph 3 of the order. And do you see under order paragraph 3: "Any attack on cultural property or other protected buildings, churches, historical monuments, medical institutions and suchlike is strictly forbidden? Do you see that. It says: "Except where the JNA units come under fire from such buildings." Do you see that first sentence? And then it lays out a plan: "In such cases, the responsible officer shall, prior to opening fire, and in a suitable manner, warn the opposite side to cease firing and leave the building." And then it continues: "Immediately submit a comprehensive report on any instance where the opening fire of protected buildings could not have been avoided. Where possible, such cases should be documented, photographs, video-recordings, witness statements, and suchlike." Were you present at any time when contact was made to the Croatians asking them to remove any weapons?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I'm a witness who can only describe what happened and what I observed at the time. I can't give you any statements that could be used as evidence or as documents. I was merely observing. I'm not sure exactly how orders were issued and received. I'm only telling you about what I understood. This here, every year, the army of Yugoslavia and Crna Gora goes through this on purely humanitarian grounds, how soldiers are treated, and that's what I did at every single point in time. I have been familiarised on a number of different occasions with General Strugar's order that fire was not to be opened on Dubrovnik, under any circumstances. I was well aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you were well aware of General Strugar's order that fire was not to be opened under any circumstances, and you had seen similar orders to this which indicates the actions that have to be taken prior to opening fire, and that's right from the command staff in Belgrade? You had seen this before, this type of document before?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something you read.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you were not present at any time when any contact was made to the Croatian side asking them to remove any weapons or we'll have to fire on the Old Town? You weren't present for any contact of that kind?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in no position to be present. I had left my observation post and I was totally cut off from everyone. The only way I could have heard about this was by talking to someone, but I was simply in no position to hear about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you never heard about anything like that either?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I've been clear enough on this one. I've been clear enough. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No. Thank you. Now, let's move on, sir. You served as an artillery observer -- first, you served as a battery commander of the 130-millimetre guns?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allow me to clarify this. I had been re-subordinated to the battalion commander, Captain Kovacevic, in order to provide fire support for the taking of the Srdj elevation, as I said yesterday. Therefore, I was no observer. I was there to provide firing support to take the Srdj elevation. I was there to help correct our tactical position. That was my role.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that role is an artillery observer. You served in the role of an artillery observer on that morning.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My role was that of artillery support.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And in that role of artillery support, your function, according to what you said yesterday, was to assist in directing fire, if your guns were going to be used?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My own fire. Yes, that's correct. I was directing the fire that was coming from my weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And your job also would have been to locate targets, because you were in a position where you could see what was happening?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's clear enough. Targets for my fire were provided by the officer that I was re-subordinated to, which was Captain Kovacevic. Those were the only targets that I was authorised to hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you had to notify your guns as to coordinates or the targets?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And if firing did in fact occur from your guns, it was your job to observe the shells to see if they were coming close to the target? That would have been your job if your guns would be firing?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that much is certain. My pieces were opening fire. I was exercising command over my guns and I was in control of that fire. That was my job and that was my right. I was there. I was in the area where the targets were. I was near the Srdj elevation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 16, line 5, the translation was erroneous, because the witness actually said if my pieces had been opening fire, not my pieces were opening fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So if your pieces had been opening fire, it was your job to make corrections, to make modifications, so you would -- so the fire would be closer to the target, you'd be honing in on the target; isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is very clear, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the reason that you're making corrections is that you don't want to be hitting objects other than the target. You don't want to be hitting churches, you don't want to be hitting cultural property, you don't want to be hitting civilian objects, you don't want to be hitting your own troops. Those are the reasons that you make corrections so you don't hit objects other than the target; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reasons for me to fire is to destroy a firing point. Of course, I need to have all my coordinates calculated very accurately because those were densely populated targets and this is a very delicate case of firing. You had to prepare really well. You had to sight the cannons well, train them well and dig them in well so as to avoid errors. These were express orders from my superior command. I had to have good insights as to what my target was, how close it was, and that's why I always stayed in the area of my targets, near my targets, so that I could make accurate corrections, and the reason that you gave is only one of the reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But you agree with that reason. You don't want to hit undesirable spots or objects; you want to hone in on the target?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. And if you're shelling and you're missing the target, the observer has to act. He can't just sit there. He has to make modifications and changes if you're not hitting the target. He can't sit back or she can't sit back and just ignore the situation.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the observer who is in charge of the firing?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Correct. The observer has to act; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. The observer who is in charge of the firing must act.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you know that because of dispersion of shells, other damage can be caused, you want to hit the target as quick as possible, or as soon as possible, and neutralise it?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's only logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you don't want to continue firing for six to ten hours because you're going to cause a lot of damage. You want to hit your target and end.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. But this is hypothetical. There are many ifs and buts. What I did is what I did. I believe I stated it with sufficient clarity. It should be clear by now. In combat operations up to that point, I had targeted firing points with a minimum use of shells. My gun was being used as a sniper. I will use this opportunity to say the following: If I'd been given the target that I had observed at the beginning of the war, none of this would have happened. I spotted a target outside the town walls, left of the Libertas Hotel, two mortars firing on Srdj and that caused a lot of damage on Srdj.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you said realising how congested the situation is, you had to be delicate, you said before in one of your answers, as part of your planning. And so you understand, sir, that in a very congested area like the Old Town, firing into that for a six- to ten-hour period, shelling that is going to cause a lot of damage because of its congested, compact nature?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And then also, sir, you realise that if you shell a compact and congested area for a period of six to ten hours, and if that area has very old or ancient buildings, there's going to be extensive damage?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And further, if there's a lot of people living there in this congested area, living close together, if you shell for six to ten hours, it's logical that people are going to get hurt?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, you're telling me something that has nothing to do with me. I understand that an impression must be made upon the Chamber, but I really have nothing to do with this. I've said it a number of times already that this is only logical. Obviously you have an explosive falling on a densely populated area. Of course it's going to cause damage. I think that much is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And it's going to cause injury to people, to civilians living there?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's move to what you were doing on the 6th of December. You said you arrived at Zarkovica at about 6.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, just before 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And eventually you went to the observation post?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The moment I arrived at the observation post, I checked the communication with my unit and reported to Captain Kovacevic, or rather, I re-subordinated myself to Captain Kovacevic. He was at that point in time my superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, this observation post was located diagonally to the left, behind the recoilless guns or the recoilless cannons or recoilless guns?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The recoilless gun was to my right. Between myself and the recoilless gun there was a hunting lodge and then the gun. That's where it was positioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you were diagonally behind the recoilless guns in the observation post?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd say that I was by its side. It wasn't diagonal. It was side by side. We were both looking the same way, towards Srdj, Dubrovnik, or rather, Srdj. That was our area of observation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In the diagram that you drew yesterday, you had yourselves behind the recoilless guns. Were you located behind the recoilless guns but to the side? So they were to the right of you?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the right. Well, perhaps the drawing was not too accurate, but that's how it was. There was a small hunting lodge just next to me and they were behind the lodge. There was a wall that had an opening. A recoilless gun was positioned on the table. And the barrel was trained on Srdj through that opening in the wall. In that wall we had three or four of those. You have the wall, the small hunting lodge, and then my position. It's like a sequence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How far were you behind the wall? How far were you set back from the wall? How many metres?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The wall ended at the hunting lodge, and then you had a flight of steps between my position and the lodge, and then a concrete clearing or area, and then you have some sort of a shelter made of stone, behind which I positioned the artillery, binoculars, a radio set, and I was there with another soldier. There was the wall, there was the hunting lodge, then the stairs, and then my position. If you mean how far the recoilless gun was from my position, between 25 and 30 metres to the right from where I was. But between myself and the recoilless gun there was the hunting lodge. Therefore, optically it was not possible to see through.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, were you in a tower? Were you inside a building? Where was this observation post that you were using to look down in the Old Town? Were you on ground level?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, of course. I was outside. And I was out in the open, totally. That's where I was wounded a month before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you were on the ground outside, approximately 20 -- 25 to 30 metres behind the edge of the wall at the edge of Zarkovica, so you were 25 to 30 feet back, outside, on the ground; that's correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Metres, not feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sorry about that. Metres. Now, are you aware that Zarkovica -- the distance from Zarkovica to the Old Town is approximately 23 to 2.500 metres?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you testified yesterday that without using binoculars you were able to see an anti-aircraft gun and a mortar.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the mortar, you testified, was outside the Old Town, between the wall and the water?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Outside the Old Town? The walls are a part of the Old Town for me, just like anything else. When looking from where I was, there's the gate, there's the walls. I have this photographic memory. I'm telling you what I remember. This mortar was, at this one particular point and then it was brought to this sort of plateau where the ships were tied, and there was a pier there and that is where it was supposed to fire from. But I did not notice it firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You never saw it fire, this mortar?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was focused on another point.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you also saw with your naked eye, in addition to seeing the mortar, you saw the anti-aircraft gun. And was that --

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And was that at the entrance to the Old Town? It wasn't clear yesterday where that gun was located. It seemed like you were saying the entrance, at the entrance, or to the right of the entrance, or left.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look at the entrance into the Old Town, to the right, if I can remember, there are some steps and there is a tower. He was up there. And from up there, he could fire. I think it's less than 2.000 metres. I don't know why I think it's less. But he was supposed to fire at Bosanka from there, or rather, at Srdj. From that tower. That was his sector. And that is the kind of opening he had. So he was on this tower near the entrance into the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And with the naked eye, you testified, without binoculars, you were able to see both of these weapons?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: With the Court's permission, may the witness be shown portions of video P66?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could he be shown a section from 21 minutes and 28 seconds to 21 minutes and 30 seconds, and stop at 30 seconds, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise that picture, Zarkovica, the Old Town being seen from Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm sorry, but --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that's the view, sir, from the recoilless guns at Zarkovica, right from the wall at the edge, looking down on the Old Town harbour?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you can see the harbour from that photograph, but you can't see it very clearly, can you, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's not a very good picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you can't see the boats, or you can't see any boats clearly from that photograph, from that view?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't see Stradun, you can't see the house. It's a very bad picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That view, from that view, you can't see any people?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't even see the hand of the observer properly, the one right in front. It's simply a bad picture. You can't even see Srdj, which was readily discernible then.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And from that view of almost two and a half kilometres away, you can't see anything clearly?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that, first and foremost, this photograph is a very bad photograph. I could see much better from that point than what you can see in this photograph. Over here, you cannot even see the hand clearly, or anything else in the background. This is not proper evidence. From there you can see perfectly Babin Kuk, you could see the tennis courts. I used binoculars, artillery binoculars too. You could see buildings, Stradun, the streets off Stradun. You could see perfectly the boats in the harbour. You could see how many of them were. Here you cannot see where the town begins and ends. This is simply a bad photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let's take another picture, sir. Let's move to 13 minutes to 13 minutes and 15 seconds.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The resolution of this photograph is very poor. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: 13 minutes to 13 minutes and 15 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you stop here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, here is another view. You recognise that's a recoilless cannon on top of Zarkovica and it's overlooking the Old Town, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And again, you can't see anything clearly in the harbour that's almost two and a half kilometres away, can you, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a camera view. The resolution is so poor that these little squares -- I mean, even a technically illiterate person would know what this is all about. This cannot be used as evidence. You cannot see anything here. But sir, I saw the things I told you about very well, very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, this camera --

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't mean anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: This camera has a zoom lens. Let's watch it zoom in and then we'll see what you can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Stop there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you've zoomed in with a zoom lens. Can you now see the harbour clearly?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Can you see each of the boats clearly?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Can you determine the size of the boats?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. At that moment, what I saw, I saw. Of course you can see whether they are small fishing boats, whether they're yachts, bigger ones were here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... the boats? No, you can't. Can you --

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say I couldn't. At this moment, of course I cannot. I can count them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: With a zoom lens, you can now, using a zoom lens, you can now count them. Can you see any people? Can you even tell if there's any people there?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I cannot make any claims to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Can you identify any of the streets in the Old Town from there, other than the Stradun?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is inappropriate cross-examination. This material, which is of such poor quality that practically nothing can be discerned, I think that it is wrong to pursue this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness said what he had to say, and if there is a clear picture, show it to the witness. But if there is a computer picture only, and if -- and the resolution is much poorer and it comes from TV Montenegro, but then if they do have proper TV footage, then perhaps the witness can be shown that. Otherwise, all of this just confuses the witness, so it is improper. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber can assess those matters when it comes to weigh the effect of the cross-examination. Carry on, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you can't discern the various streets and buildings in the Old Town, can you, in that photograph, from that view?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the Defence lawyer said, this is camera footage. What I saw, I see with my own eyes. This doesn't mean a thing. I can only say with reliability if I were to be standing on Zarkovica now, whether I can see the streets or not or whether I can count and see the boats or not. This is very poor resolution, so why are you asking me about these pictures? This is not the view I had. This is not how I could see on that day. I did not make my conclusions through this camera. I base my conclusions on my own eyesight, which is much better, and also the angle of the sun was different. This was 10.00 or 11.00 or perhaps even later. The basis of this I cannot --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You're saying that your eyesight is better than the zoom lens on that camera?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I object. Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, the cross-examination is proper. We are conscious of the matters you are putting and we can weigh it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, the question is: Are you saying that your eyesight is better than the zoom lens on that camera?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was quite clear. Yes. And I was 12 or 13 years younger, at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you were also 25 to 30 metres behind the recoilless cannons, where those pictures are being taken from. Let's move on for 15 more seconds.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not behind. I was not behind. Please take that into account.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Stop again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Again, sir, from that distance, can you see any people, and can you determine any of the streets went within the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I've already given you an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: My question is: Can you see any people or can you determine or see any streets within the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the position where I viewed this, I could see that. This position shows the ramparts. You cannot even see Stradun. You cannot see the entrance into town. You cannot see the positions on the left of the mortar and on the right of the anti-aircraft tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you continue.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could see far more clearly than what you can see in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And at this position, sir, can you discern any of the streets within the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, not a thing can be seen in this picture. Buildings cannot be seen, let alone streets.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that, sir, is because Zarkovica is approximately two and a half kilometres from the Old Town harbour; isn't that correct? That's why you can't see it?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what you say. You cannot see through the lens of this camera, but I saw it clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that everybody else said what I said too, that I saw what I saw clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. Let us continue. You said you saw a mortar and an anti-aircraft gun with the naked eye and that they were not firing; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not observe any firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And, sir, you said that the -- that these were out in the open, they were clearly visible; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And how long had the mortar been there? You said it was moved from one place to another place and then you don't know where it got moved to. How long had it been there, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me explain. They did not move it from one place to another. They would put it into a shelter and then they will take it out from the place where they wanted it to fire. It was all planned. Obviously, for that mortar, they made a sector of activity. And it had only one --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you can't answer for what their plans were. My question to you is: How long was that mortar visible? That's all. Five minutes, ten minutes, four minutes, fifteen minutes?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The moment when it was noticed, fire was opened at it, as far as I can remember. But my priority was - I'm telling you this yet again - the place that Captain Nesic showed me through binoculars, and that was the mortars next to Libertas. That's why I asked for fire and that's why I spoke to my command a few times and I had orders issued. This was within their range and I did not really pay attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. So you don't know how long it had been there. Can you estimate any amount of time - five minutes, ten minutes - that you had seen it exposed there?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you again: This was not the focus of my attention. But it was not usable any longer after that, so it wasn't there. This firing point could have been eliminated, and it was eliminated. I mean, well, eliminated. It simply was not active.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You saw this mortar, and it was --

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And again -- yes. I've already said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And it was exposed. You saw it with the open eye. It was in the clear, this mortar. Was the crew also standing there in the clear, exposed?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course they pushed it out there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you see them standing by it, a group of men?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a largish group near the entrance into the Old Town. All right. That doesn't matter now. But at any rate, they had to be there. There had to be personnel around the mortar, and there were personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You said there had to be and there were but you just didn't see them, or you don't recall if you saw them?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, it's logical. If the mortar is there, they had to push it out there. I was not out there to establish whether there was someone there or whether there was not anyone there. If the mortar is there, of course it had to be pulled out. At that moment -- or rather, let's not get too confused. It was pulled out of this particular point. That's the only place from where they could get it. This was in the morning, around 8.00 in the morning. All these objectives that I talked about were noticed. After that, I focused on my own objective. After that, I no longer paid attention to this. I just know that fire was opened, and I know that there was heavy smoke there, and as far as I know, after that, this was not a priority either for Captain Kovacevic or the others. Libertas was their priority. So that objective was not active.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And in addition, according to your testimony, to the mortar that was open and exposed, there was also an anti-aircraft gun that was visible, open, and exposed; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And when I say "exposed," you were looking down upon this right from Zarkovica, on these weapons?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, yes. Well, that's what I'm telling you. That's the only thing I'm telling you, what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So the Croatians placed two weapons in open view of their enemy, or their opposing army. That's what you're trying to say, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not the way you put it so that it would be in open view of their enemy. They had to put it out there so that it could fire. They could not shoot from a room. And it simply had to be there. It had to fire from out in the open. It could not fire from the point where it was originally. They did not put it out there so that it would be in the open view of their enemy. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So the Croatians put two weapons within open view of you and the other soldiers on Zarkovica, within the view of the JNA troops?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two, and the two next to Libertas, that makes four, and that's what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We're not talking about Libertas right now, which is a distance away. We're talking about those two weapons which you claim to have seen. Those were placed, according to your testimony, right out in the open, directly in front of the opposing army. That's your testimony.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In front of our troops, they were there at 8.00 in the morning. Later on, I heard from my colleagues that the cannon had been active. I did not hear about the mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And sir, were you aware that the Old Town had been shelled in October of 1991?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that the Old Town had been shelled in November of 1991?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that the Old Town harbour had been shelled in November of 1991?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that the boats in the Old Town harbour and the walls that are adjacent to the harbour had been shelled in November of 1991?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As far as I can remember, all of that happened in December.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you aware that Maljutkas or wire-guided missiles struck the harbour area, the boats and the walls of the Old Town in November of 1991?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But you're saying that the Croats placed two weapons in an area, which two weapons exposed to everyone in an area that had previously been shelled?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you keep on talking about your role. While you were up there, it was your job to observe and direct your weapons if they had in fact fired.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you indicated that your weapons were quite precise. That's what you testified to yesterday, as to the --

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you know that some weapons are more precise than others.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. Of course. It depends on the length of the barrel, the weight of the shell, the combination of the barrel and the emplacement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you're aware that there are both direct and indirect-fire weapons, direct --

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Direct and indirect. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you're also aware, sir, that there were various weapons available to the JNA on Zarkovica and elsewhere on the morning of December 6, 1991; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. But what do you mean when you're referring to difference, when you're saying "various"?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, within the 2nd Operational Group, they had different kinds of weapons, such as Maljutka missiles. You knew that there were Maljutka missiles up on Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, and I said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You knew that there were recoilless cannons up on Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. And I even drew that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Correct. And you thought that there might have been a Zolja, what you call a Zolja or a Zolja, some Zoljas up on Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Zolja cannot be used at such distances. It's useless. A Zolja's range is up to 400 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you're also aware that there were tanks also used in the action?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: On both sides of Srdj?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you're also aware that there were 120-millimetre mortars used and available?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see them in the area of Zarkovica and Brgat.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Not Zarkovica, but elsewhere the JNA had those available?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course. It had 130-millimetre guns and 122-millimetre guns and 105-millimetre guns. The 9th VPS had all of that. Now, what the others had, I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, there were also sniper rifles available. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are infantry weapons that played no role whatsoever on the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But they were available?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, if you can see a target and you're within range of a target, you can neutralise it?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And if something is exposed, it's even easier to neutralise with a direct-fire weapon, if an object is exposed, a military target is exposed, as opposed to one that's hidden; it's much easier to neutralise?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Could the interpreters please repeat this. The first sentence. I did not understand your first sentence. If something is exposed, and could they please continue now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If a target is exposed, is in the open, it's much easier --

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. All right. Yes. I understand now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the anti-aircraft gun was never destroyed, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Destroyed? I don't know. I just know that later on -- actually, it was hit by a Maljutka and I think it was destroyed, neutralised. It was hit by a Maljutka, and I think that it was destroyed. I saw smoke later, so it was a Maljutka that had hit it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But you're not certain. You think; you're not certain.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mean, if I were on the very spot, that is the only way I could have known whether it was eliminated or not. I just know that the mortar was no longer active and it was no longer the object of my observation. It was not active afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the mortar was never destroyed?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The place was hit where it was, but it was neutralised. It wasn't active after that. And the right effect was achieved. You don't have to destroy something to attain your goals and finish firing at your target. The main thing was that it wasn't active afterwards. It wasn't operational afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, the fact that it wasn't destroyed and then you're not certain that the anti-aircraft gun was destroyed, and these weapons had been in the open, isn't that because they never existed? Isn't that why they weren't destroyed?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not how it was. Hardly. Those weapons did exist there. That is absolutely certain. They would cover with fire and then after that the cannon was active, judging by what my colleagues told me, and I think that the mortar wasn't active at all. The mortar wasn't active at all. And that's where all the activity ceased, for those artillery pieces of the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But you, with the naked eye, as you saw them previously, never saw them destroyed; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said: They weren't operational after that. They weren't active. There were no mortars there any more. They were neutralised. That's what that means.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Assuming they ever existed to begin with.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, we saw pictures of Zarkovica. As you know, Zarkovica overlooks the general area of the Old Town and the area --

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Old Town and Babin Kuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And it's an unobstructed view. There's nothing in the way. There's nothing blocking your view.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we saw it on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you can see the walls of the Old Town and you can see the Old Town in the distance, you can see it somewhat generally with the naked eye, but you could also see it clearer with binoculars and sighting devices?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can. Just a moment. I'm not getting the text, the LiveNote, up on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you looked down on the Old Town during the day on several occasions? From Zarkovica, you looked down on the Old Town on several occasions?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was spread out in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, an observation. Perhaps an irrelevant one, but I would nonetheless like to state it, with respect to what it says on page 36, line 16 and 17. The witness does not mention any LiveNote or anything like that. I don't know where that comes from.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't got a picture of the text, the translation, again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you have the translation of the transcript in front of you now on the monitor?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's working now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, how long were you in Zarkovica during that day, sir? You were there just before 6.00. Until what time?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until before dark. 4.00, half past 4.00, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And during the day, while you're on the Old Town, did you see smoke rising from the town, large amounts of smoke?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you see clouds of smoke over the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you see thick, black smoke coming from the boats rising above the harbour?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. That was what was targeted. The mortar, with the Maljutka.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you see thick, black smoke rising above the boats?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did see thick, black smoke. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And all that smoke hovering over the Old Town, that affected the visibility that you had into the Old Town streets?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And that was the effect of the mortar at the spot where it was supposed that the observed one was located. So the mortar over the roofs of the houses, and that smoke came from that, around the streets where the mortar was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Are you saying the smoke in the Old Town came from these flashes which you believe to be a mortar? All the smoke in the Old Town came from that mortar that you believe to have been in the Old Town? Is that what you're saying? The clouds of smoke?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think you understood me correctly. The smoke was the result of the falling of shells, mortar shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fall of shells. And the flashes occurred before that. Before that, you had the flashes of light from the firing of the shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, could you see buildings burning in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I saw smoke coming from the roofs, so the smoke was caused by the flames. I didn't see an open flame, but quite obviously the roofs had been set fire to, because there was smoke coming out of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you see the boats burning?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you see flames coming from the boats?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course. Where there's smoke, there's fire. You couldn't have had smoke coming out of something cold.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you see shells striking and then smoke rising after a shell, a mortar shell, struck an area?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I saw the falling of the shells on the boats in the small harbour where these two targets were observed, so that was the result of the Maljutka, whereas the small street from where we saw, observed the firing of the mortar, they hit the roofs and of course the roofs were destroyed. It was set fire to. And the result of all that was the smoke coming out.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you use your binoculars or the sighting equipment as you looked at the Old Town during the shelling?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And using your binoculars, could you see the holes in the roofs?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They weren't holes in the roofs. It was the whole roof falling in. Even if they were new roofs, they would have been destroyed. They weren't holes; they were whole chunks of roofs.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, would you like me to take a break at this time or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, if that's a convenient point. We will adjourn until 10 to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good morning again, Mr. Pepic.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: By the way, you're still a member of the military, the Yugoslav national army?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, as I said at the beginning of my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And your current rank is major, did you say? I'm sorry, what was your current rank? No. It was captain?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lieutenant colonel. Captain of the frigate, in naval terms. If you compare that to the army, the rank would be lieutenant colonel of the infantry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. Now, as we left off, you had indicated that whole chunks of roofs had caved in or collapsed, and buildings in the Old Town; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, parts of roofs. Because they were small surface areas, small roofs, four corners. So yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you could see --

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Caved in. That would be exactly it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you could see that with the binoculars. You could see these caved-in roofs?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you also see the -- in the Stradun or in the streets of the Old Town roofs tiles, debris, clutter along the streets? Could you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you could see damage --

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you could see damaged buildings?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Principally roofs, as I have said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you could see that some of the houses of worship were damaged?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know specifically -- well, yes. Churches. I had heard that the Orthodox Church had been destroyed, which is the other side of Stradun. I heard that that had been set fire to.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you see people in the streets at various times running through the streets?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see people at any time, with the naked eye or with binoculars either. And as far as I heard, at about 6.00, the alarm was sounded. A general alert was sounded. I didn't hear that myself, but that's what people told me, for an air strike, air danger, and people took to the shelters, having heard the alarm sound. So apart from the movement of these artillery pieces and the crews -- in Lokrum, I didn't see people at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you never saw any dead bodies in the street or any injured persons lying in the street. You were never able to see it during the times that you watched or the times that you observed the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 6th, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, when it became dark or you left just as it was becoming dark, could you see the burning buildings in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you see the flames rising above the buildings?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I said, there's no smoke without fire. The roof constructions were on fire, and so was the material underneath. And there was debris, scattered stones, tiles in the streets.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you could see the smoke covering much of the Old Town at that point, darkness and the smoke covering much of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't dark. There wasn't darkness. It was dark when I left the observation post, as I said, 4.00, half past 4.00. When it really got dark was round a quarter to 5.00. So as it was getting dark, I wasn't -- I couldn't see that, so I couldn't compare.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And prior to December 6th, when the JNA shelled the Old Town, you had never seen it in such condition; fires, debris in the streets, smoke above the -- clouds of smoke above the town? You had never seen the Old Town in that condition prior to December 6, 1991?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of the fact that the Old Town was shelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You had no knowledge that the Old Town --

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I didn't see it at all. That is quite certain. I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You did not see the shelling of the Old Town on December 6th, 1991? We're talking about December 6th.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I did see. Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Prior to December 6th, had you ever seen the Old Town in that type of condition: Houses burning, roofs collapsed, buildings damaged, churches damaged, debris in the streets? Had you ever seen the Old Town in that condition prior to December 6, 1991?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was quite resolute in saying that I did not see that, nor do I have any information about that, before the 6th of December. On the 6th of December, I saw what I described to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that's what I'm saying --

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The consequences.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Prior to December 6th, you had never seen the Old Town in that condition? No.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, I'd like to show you portions of a videotape, again, P66, with the Court's approval. Just portions of a videotape relating to December 6th. Could we go to 31 minutes and 15 seconds, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise the photograph in front of you as being the Old Town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you can see at that time that there's already a cloud of smoke over much of the Old Town; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already described all this. I described having seen this previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that's what it looked like. 7.47 in the morning, there was already a cloud of smoke over the Old Town; isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7.45 in the morning, you say? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: 7.47 in the morning. Would you like me to take it back a few seconds? Would you like to see the tape again? All I'm saying: Is that consistent with your view with binoculars at approximately 7.47 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this firing, but as far as I know, that started after about half past 8.00, 9.00. What we see on the picture, I saw that afterwards, but not before 8.00. And I remember exactly, because at 800 hours, I observed the targets we're talking about, although all this activity started earlier on, at around 6.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you take it back to 31 minutes and 15 seconds, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Stop right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
