utterances.text: You can see the smoke rising over the Old Town. What time does it indicate on December 12th -- I'm sorry, December 6th, 1991? 7.47 a.m.?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, no point of objection can be made at the present. I'm getting concerned at the extent to which your objections tend to put words in the witness's mouth. That's why I'm being -- restraining you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can present my objection even if the witness leaves the courtroom. I don't know how to proceed. But I really do have an objection with respect to the contents this footage. If -- well, if you won't allow me, I won't present it. But I have a relevant objection, so I don't know how to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is an exhibit that is before us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The problem is -- yes, of course, that is right, Your Honour. However, there's nothing tying the time to the footage itself as evidence. That is the basis for my objection. Of course, the footage is there as evidence, but the time and how it is interconnected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That issue is being explored at the present time with the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you see the time listed on that video, 7.47 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The time is listed. It's printed out.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And at that time, you already see smoke over the Old Town and shells have hit the Old Town, isn't that correct, according to this video and the time listed therein?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you chronologically. I'm quite sure that it happened at 8.00. At 8.00, I was shown the target at Lokrum, from where the shooting came from, around the Libertas Hotel. I asked to be allowed to open fire. I was not allowed to do so. So that was just after 8.00, as I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. You've made that statement.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same thing that you can see on the footage here, that situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But you do note, sir, that it indicates prior to 8.00 the Old Town has already been shelled and there is smoke rising from the buildings in the Old Town, prior to 8.00? Isn't that correct? Isn't that what's on the video?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it says 7.47, it doesn't mean that it's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All I'm saying is: Isn't that what's on the video? If it is, yes; if it isn't, say no.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you can see, but I state again: At 8.00, or that is to say, 13 minutes after this situation, the firing still hadn't started. It started after 8.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's continue with the video. If you watch closely.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you just saw the times, 9.34 in the morning and 9.39, and at those points you can see clouds of smoke over the Old Town; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And obviously, that's going to affect your visibility from Zarkovica as you look towards the Old Town, isn't that correct, even using binoculars?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's quite clear, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Can we continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And when you talked about boats on fire in the harbour and smoke coming up from those boats, that's consistent with your testimony, isn't it, sir, the boats burning?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You can see that black smoke rising up, which again affects your visibility, the black smoke, that thick, black smoke from the boats?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could we continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, if we go back: Did you see the missile hit right over the turret and then cause a puff of smoke? Let's go back to 31:50. You watch right over the turret. Do you see the flash too? Did you see the flash and then the puff of smoke?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the smoke, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you see the flash before that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat that, please. Show it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If you watch right over that turret.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've just seen it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that was at approximately 31:51. Now, could we move to 32:13.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Stop right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you can see what the Old Town looks like at 12.44 p.m. Is that consistent with your memory of what it looks like, clouds of smoke over the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And at that point, it's very poor visibility for an observer, even with binoculars and sighting equipment?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If we continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And as we continue in the afternoon, black smoke covers most of the sky, or much of the sky over the Old Town; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And if we move to 33:05, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could my learned friend tell me the date of this last footage that we just saw. I don't want to suggest or lead. Could you tell us that last still that was shown, what date is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All this footage together is December 6th. Could you continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And sir, you can see at 4.33 in the afternoon, there's still clouds of smoke over the Old Town, and that's approximately the time you were leaving; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And finally, 33:20 to 33:28, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: To 38, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And when you said you could see the Old Town in flames just when nightfall was beginning, or it was at dusk, that's what it looked like? You could see flames and smoke coming from the houses in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly like that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And it was an ugly scene, to say the least?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A terrible scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. No more video is necessary at this time. I just have a question as to views of certain areas. If the witness could be shown P11 just for a quick moment. Sir, you indicated that you had been to the Old Town on several occasions. Do you see those hotels overlooking the Adriatic, the Argentina, I think the Excelsior, those hotels overlooking? Are you familiar with those? Do you recall those from your trips and visits to the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Belvedere is the first one, the Argentina Hotel was to the left. Just up the road, I've never been to the new hotels at Babin Kuk. I usually drove straight to the Old Town. But yes, I am familiar with the Argentina and Belvedere hotels. I know about the hotel district at Babin Kuk. I know about the Libertas Hotel. I don't know about this stretch here, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you knew that those hotels had either, if you want to call them cafes or bars, and different patio-type areas overlooking the water, as well as the rooms had balconies overlooking the water? At the Argentina. Let's start off with that one.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Argentina, if that's the one I think it is, it was a bit recessed back from the sea and it had a view on Zarkovica, but it had a view on the sea, right there also. It was just off the road, on a slope, facing the sea.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And from that Argentina Hotel you could also see the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. No further need of the map. Thank you. Just one other quick question before we continue. What was your rank in December of 1991, on December 6th?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a captain back then.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you testified yesterday about seeing flashes, and you identified on a diagram this morning two streets. You weren't sure which one, but two streets that you had seen flashes. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't see on two streets. It was either one or the other. But that's only an assumption that I have made. Because from my position, from which I was looking, as I said yesterday, my line of observation was parallel to the Stradun. Those streets, in relation to where I was, you know, I couldn't keep a sense of distance how far the streets were from one another. And in relation to the Stradun, whether it was in the nearer half or in the further half.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But what you said was you saw some of -- you saw these flashes. And did you see them --

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: -- Just in the morning or throughout the day or in different periods of the day, once an hour? When did you see them, and how often?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it in the morning. The firing was observed in the morning, and then later on, you have seen for yourselves, after all, when the mortar started firing on them, it was very difficult to observe that. They targeted the spots where it should have been. But let me make this clear. The part that you could see from Strincjera is a section that I couldn't see from where I was, whether there was anything there. I'm only telling you about what I saw, as to any firing by the Croatian side.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's all we want to deal with, is what you saw. So you saw some flashing on that street off the Stradun. When you saw the flashing, did you see it reflecting off the top of a building? Because you said it was -- whatever the object was, it was between two buildings. So unless you're Superman, you can't see through the buildings. Did you see flashing way up along the top of the building?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you're aware, sir, that --

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The flash that I saw was from the bottom up, and then it was moving, the place which I assume was not exposed, well, I didn't really have a view. It was recessed behind the corner, the right-hand corner, and looking at the opposite side, at the left corner, that's where I saw the flash and it was moving up.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you could just see the flash along -- if there are two buildings, it would be the back building along the top of the back building, the rear building?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, from where you were on Zarkovica, from the rooftop down, how much of the building could you see? Are we talking about a metre, maybe a metre and a half? Because there is a building in front and you could see the rear building. So what would you say that you could see from the top of Zarkovica? A metre, a metre and a half down, two metres?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the roof down, I really can't say. I think all the buildings were more or less the same height, but I don't think that's relevant. In terms of what I saw, it was this ratio between the buildings. It was sideways. It wasn't about the height of the buildings; it was about the angle at which they were facing one another. I saw the flash from here. It was a bit protruded because my angle of vision was a bit askew, in a manner of speaking, and I was watching Stradun from this sort of angle, and that was the angle from which I saw these two buildings. I think all the buildings along the Stradun were more or less the same height. I didn't notice any major discrepancies in terms of height, or at least not that I can think of right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But the flashing that you saw was high -- you said at the top of the building. So are you saying you saw a flash between one metre from the roof down one metre, or maybe two metres down from the top of the roof?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... saw it along the top or did you see it along the side. Do you want to change your testimony and say you now saw the flashing on the side? Yesterday you said you saw it along the top.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that yesterday. I was very resolute in what I said. I saw a flash between the buildings, and it was flaring up from the bottom up, moving up.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But sir, if there was a building between the building that you were looking at, you couldn't see --

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it caught the top of the building too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What could you see? Where did you see the flash? Did you see it along the top or did you see it somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I saw it at the bottom of the building. It was from the level of the Stradun, the street. This piece of equipment was at the bottom, and that's where the flame was coming from and it was spreading up and I saw the building further down, in a manner of speaking. I can't say if it was one metre or a metre and a half away from there, but it was on that side, in that particular shadow, that I saw the flame spreading upwards. You showed me the shell fall and you saw how the flame was spreading, the flash was spreading. The same way from the spot where the shell fell then, that's the way the flash came. It falls down and then it flares up suddenly. It only take a fraction of a second for the flash to start moving up. But it wasn't from the top of the building. It was from the street level. That's what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour -- I apologise. Something to do with the interpretation. The interpretation is inadequate, and the witness is making a comparison there which is not reflected. Therefore, he just made a comparison which is not reflected in the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you see any particular problem in the recording of your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not that familiar with the language, really. I am slightly familiar with the language, but not sufficiently.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May I question or would the Court like to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you want to explore that further, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you indicated when a shell falls, you just said, there's a flash; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When a missile falls, there's a flash; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And after that you have smoke, and then the fragmentation of a shell. You have rubble on all sides, and debris.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the explosion itself is much more powerful, or the sound, at least, than when it's being fired, but the flame at the mouth of the barrel and when the shell falls and the flash.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And we had in fact seen on the video, we saw a flash and then smoke rising. We saw a missile hit, a flash, and then smoke rising. So when we talk about flashes, there's a lot of different types of objects that can cause a flash; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Like I said, this sort of flash can be caused by the falling of a shell, or rather, the firing of a shell. I don't see what else could have caused a flash like that. I really can't think of anything else that could, not the kind of flash that I saw, at least, except for what I said. And I confirm this in my conversations with my colleagues, who observed the same thing. So that's what I'm trying to say. My information has been confirmed. That's what I'm saying. Perhaps I would challenge this information had I seen myself --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You said --

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... perhaps you would challenge it if you had seen it yourself. What was that again, sir? You had said: "Perhaps I would challenge ...."

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So if I had seen it for myself -- my impression was it could only have been caused by that, but if two other people have confirmed this, and the old wisdom says that two people know more than one person alone. Therefore two people saw this, then it must be true.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What you indicated was you saw a flash, and based on the flash that you saw at different times, you said you made an assumption that it was a mortar firing; isn't that correct? That's what you've testified --

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could not have been any other artillery weapon. It would not have been possible for anything else to be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... assumption that you made, based on seeing a flash, was that it was a mortar firing; isn't that correct? That was your testimony.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you further testified that you never saw the object which caused the flash. You never saw that object. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All this time, throughout these two days, that's what I kept saying. I saw the flash, and that was the result of the mortar activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I want to take it step by step. You never saw the object; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And then you also admit, sir, that there are other objects that can cause a flash; isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recognise that. As I said, I have no information as to what else might have caused that sort of flash except a projectile falling there, which was not the case, or the activity of an artillery weapon. So that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's correct. There are other types of objects that could cause a flash, such as a shell landing and exploding or a missile landing and exploding; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And throughout the day, you never saw anything other than a flash out of that area, even though visibility was in fact difficult?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my previous testimony, I told you what I had seen. I told you I had seen roofs burning. I told you I had seen shells falling. So it's simply not true that I did not --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm just asking you a specific question. Because of poor visibility, all you ever saw that day was a flash on occasion; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time when I saw the flash, this flash could easily be observed. So when I saw the flash, it was possible to clearly observe it, and then from the fall of the Maljutkas, then the boats began and then I couldn't see the Stradun any more. But up to that point, I had noticed several flashes. I can't say there were three flashes. Perhaps there were three; perhaps two, perhaps five. But it certainly wasn't a single flash.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now you saw - I'll take your parameters - between two and five flashes in that area before visibility became poor; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, several.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Several. And you know that several shells struck the Old Town, several mortars shells; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not several. More.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: A large number of mortar shells struck the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And when these shells struck, they made flashes too?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Caused damage too. Fragmentation. On all sides of the construction material, there was smoke. There was the construction material flying all over the place and bursts. The sound of that burst was quite different than the one coming from the mouth of a barrel.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And when you saw these flashes, you saw them from mortars, there were also flashes when the Maljutkas struck, as we saw right on that turret. That also caused an explosion and a flash.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Therefore, a flash is the only thing connecting the fall of the shell and the launching of the shell. Everything else is different: The sound, the effect, the secondary results, so to speak. So these are two very distinct things. There was no way I could have confused those two. The fall of a shell and the launching of a shell itself, and a Maljutka. You can see the trace of it -- only the person who launches it sees the trace of a Maljutka and it develops a very high temperature. Of course there will be fire and of course the target will burn down.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And when you -- when a shell explodes behind a building, so you can see the building, all you can see is the flash as it radiates up or radiates to the side?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see the flash, you can see smoke when it falls. And as I say, you can see matter flying around.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what you saw on that date was also a flash, either radiating up, radiating diagonally, or radiating to the side?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the early morning hours, yes. Correct. Early morning hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you also admit that there's a lot of different objects that can cause flashes. A camera can cause a flash, an emergency light can cause a flash, a mortar shell can cause a flash, a Maljutka exploding can cause a flash, a shell from other weapons, artillery can cause flashes. Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a flash from the mouth of a barrel when a shell was being launched. I know that much. I'm an officer. I'm an artillery officer, and I know what a flash looks like when it's caused by a camera, by a rotating light, or by the mouth of a barrel.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But the difference, sir, is you never saw the object --

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's a huge difference between those.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But the difference, sir, is you never saw the object that made that flash; isn't that correct? You just saw the flash.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Speaking of objects, speaking of mortars, from the tip of the barrel upward, how tall is the flash when an 82-millimetre mortar fires? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This artillery piece was between the two walls.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No, no. Sir. Sir --

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe that --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... different question about an artillery piece, if you know. An 82-millimetre mortar, when it fires, the flash that comes out of the tip of the barrel, how high does it go? Does it flash for one metre high? Does it flash for two metres, three metres?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I began my answer all right. It's not the same thing, we're talking about a closed area or an open area, whether the area was limited. If the mortar had been in open field, it would have been difficult for me to notice the firing and the flash, but it was positioned between two buildings. And on the farther building you could easily notice the flame, so that's the reason I'm telling you this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about that incident right now. Right now I'm just asking you about a mortar in general, an 82-millimetre mortar. The flash, when it fires, how high does it run from the tip of the barrel upward? Are we talking about two metres up?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again, it's impossible. You can't compare a specific case. Obviously, it's different. In the night it's much longer and in daytime it's much shorter. This flash only means that the air is lighter than the surrounding light, and that's how the difference in terms of light is established. And that's that. And it's absolutely not the same thing, because this is a natural phenomenon, after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Then tell me: What is it during the day and what is it during the night? Are we talking about one metre, two metres, three metres high?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So in this specific case, practically it was six, seven metres. So that whole side of the building was lit up. It was flaring. The whole side of the building, the whole building flared up at that moment. First a dark red light and then moving down the spectrum to ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, if you have two buildings across from each other and you're looking so that you can only see the top area of the back building, you can't see the whole building light up. You can see a small portion among the top and maybe along the side, if the buildings aren't even. But you can't see that whole back wall of the building; isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said before, I saw that. I saw that part of the building. Now, precisely whether it was three, four, five metres. The other building, I did see that. And the side of the building, I could see the flame reflected there. I saw the lateral part of that building, the lateral side of the building. I never referred to the roof, to begin with.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But if you saw the lateral building and there was a building of the same height directly in front of it, you could only see the top portion of the lateral or the rear building, if you want to call it; isn't that correct? You could not see the whole wall unless you were directly over it looking down or unless you had the power of Superman, with x-ray power, to look through the building?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I don't have Superman's eyesight. I definitely don't. But as I said, the buildings did not overlap visually. They were distant enough from one another. As for the farther building, from it I saw about two, three, or four metres. That's what I saw. And the nearer building did not cover the building that was farther off visually. It did not obstruct my view. I told you that the Stradun was in my line of vision, roughly speaking, but I had that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But all you're able to do is see a flash, without the object which caused it; isn't that correct? You never saw the object which caused it? You just made an assumption about it, but you never saw it?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You've provided the answer instead of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Is that correct: You never, though, saw the object that caused it?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I showed you the document from the General Staff a while ago, from General Adzic, which warned against firing into -- against cultural or religious property, against hospitals. And at the end of it, remember that paragraph 3 or paragraph 4, it says: "If possible, take photographs. Take videos of any object prior to firing." Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall the part about recording. I know that at one point it was said that we should take shelter from the fire. General Strugar had ordered that fire not be returned, but rather that we should take shelter. And I remember General Staff something about recording, but I don't see that that changes anything in terms of the inviolability of the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you also aware, sir, that the political officer, Mihajlo Zarkovic, complained about certain Croatian propaganda, the Croats' use of propaganda? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown two documents, P116 and D78. Could we look at P116, please, paragraph 3 of the order.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You've shown me this before.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I told you that I had seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And do you see the final phrase in parentheses, or actually read the final sentence: "Wherever possible, such cases should be documented (photographs, video recordings, witness statements, and suchlike)." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will you please repeat that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sure. Do you see the final sentence of paragraph 3 of the order: "Whenever possible, such cases should also be documented (photographs, video recordings, witness statements, and suchlike)."

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And then could we look at, very quickly, D88, please, second page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did you see 88 or 78?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. D88. I'm very sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you see three paragraphs up from the bottom: "The task of the officers is to use" -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sorry about that, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you see three paragraphs from the bottom: "The task of the officers is to use specific examples to inform their men and lay bare the lives of enemy propaganda, as well as to ensure that there is no detriment affect on the morale of the units." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, from the general command, we see that they ask you that, whenever possible, to take photographs or videos of any enemy weaponry in a protected area; isn't that correct? In the previous document.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And in this document, Commander Zarkovic mentions the task is to use specific examples to inform the men and lay bare the lies of enemy propaganda. Basically, bring proof to show that the Croats are lying or using propaganda of some kind; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So while you were up on Zarkovica, while you were up on Zarkovica and you claim to have seen a mortar and you claim to have seen an anti-aircraft gun, did you photograph either weapon?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Photograph it with what?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: There was testimony that some people had cameras up there. Did you photograph any of those two weapons you claim to have seen?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some people. I was a battery commander up there, and I was observing the points with appropriate equipment. This order does not refer to me. My task, as a soldier, is to guide the fire of the battery and to command the battery. As for this, there is a special information service of the unit, and they deal with such matters, not I. I do not take photographs. I am a battery commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you see or order anyone as battery commander to take photographs of those weapons?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not have ordered anyone to do it, or would I have the right to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you ask anyone to take photographs of those weapons that you allege to have seen?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already given you an answer. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you take any videos? Did you or anyone else up on Zarkovica take any videos as to those weapons that you had seen, as required or requested by the Chief of Staff of the General Staff of the JNA? Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not asked to do that. You did not understand the order properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm just saying: Did you. Not whether you were asked. Did you, or did you see anyone else do so, as requested by the Chief of Staff of the General Staff of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, these instructions do not pertain to me and I did not do that. As far as information is concerned, documentation, whatever, except for my statement, there is nothing else, and there is no need to put any further questions to me, because the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You can sit down, Madam Usher. If you could leave D88 there, and you can just sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you claimed that you had seen flashes, which you had believed to be a mortar, in the Old Town. You claimed to have seen an anti-aircraft gun somewhere either on the walls of the Old Town or by the walls of the Old Town. Did you immediately contact your superiors to contact the Croatians to have them remove those weapons? Did you -- first, did you make any contact?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was subordinated to Captain Kovacevic. Captain Kovacevic clearly noted that, and Captain Kovacevic, I can only assume that, asked for it. I was not next to him. So what you're asking about is something that he should have done, and I think that he did do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you notify Captain Kovacevic that you had seen flashes coming from the Old Town and that you thought you had seen an anti-aircraft gun by the walls of the Old Town? Did you notify Captain Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was aware of that information before I was. I'm not the person who informed him. He had already received that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you present when Captain Kovacevic called -- made any contact to anyone to have those weapons removed?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in contact non-stop. He called non-stop, either from a mobile device or from a stationary device or from a telephone. But at any rate, he was in command that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And when you say he was in non-stop contact, would that be with the command of the 9th VPS?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as you said, I'm not Superman. I can't tell. I can't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you were never present -- or were you present for any of his conversations, by radio or telephone?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing I know as far as contacts are concerned, I was present, but I didn't hear that. They were far away enough from me not to -- for me not to be able to hear it. At any rate, Captain Kovacevic would not be talking so that everybody could hear it. I know that when he asked me for fire, I pointed at Commander Zec, and I know that he asked him for permission to fire, and I know that Captain Zec did not give him permission to fire. As for the rest, I don't know for sure who he talked to and what kind of contact it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you don't know if any contact was made that day to the Croatians to remove any potential weapons before the Old Town was shelled? You weren't present for any conversations, so you can't tell?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was present, but I wasn't listening, or I could not hear it, rather. There are people who are relevant for that matter and who can confirm whatever you need confirmed. I'm not a witness that can answer that kind of question and that can be of any benefit to you for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you basically never overheard any conversations to the Croatian side, period? No?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I mean, I'm confirming what you said. I did not. And I could not, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you do know that after -- that during the day the Old Town was shelled heavily?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We discussed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you were up on Zarkovica for most of the day, and you had --

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: -- a front-row seat, as you might call it, to the action that was occurring. You saw the shelling by the JNA of the Old Town, you saw the shelling and the attack on Srdj; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And as a result of the position that you were in, did anyone -- I'm sorry. Did anyone call you and tell you to report to the 2nd Operational Group and tell them what you had seen? Were you called to the 2nd Operational Group, the command of the 2nd Operational Group, and asked what you had seen on that day?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what this question means. I told you at the very outset that I was an officer who was subordinated to Captain Kovacevic, so my task was quite clear. I could not disregard my superior officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You were aware that there was a 2nd Operational Group and General Strugar was the commander; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you called to report to the command of the 2nd Operational Group - and this is after December 6th - to explain what you had observed on December 6th from Zarkovica? Were you ever called to the command of the 2nd Operational Group and asked to explain what you had seen on December 6th from Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you ever met or interviewed by anyone in this command of the 2nd Operational Group as to what you had seen on Zarkovica on the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you ever questioned by anyone in the 2nd Operational Group as to your role on Zarkovica on December 6th in 1991?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, it makes no sense that anybody from the command of the 2nd Operational Group would ask me what I was doing there. I was doing my professional work, which is clearly spelled out. It's not of my own free will that I came there by accident. I was sent there to carry out an assignment. And according to the regulations pertaining to the use of a battery, it is well known what I did there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What I'm just asking you is: Did anyone from the 2nd Operational Group ask you what you did on that day? Did anyone come and ask you or have you place in writing what you had done on that day? It's a yes-or-no question.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did anyone, as part of an investigation, ever speak to you after December 6th, anyone? It doesn't even have to be in the 2nd Operational Group, concerning what happened on that day, concerning your observations? Did anyone contact you and interview you?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Who interviewed you?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Admiral Jokic, a year ago. I'm sure that he provided you with a copy of that, or I cannot be sure, but I think he did. I was supposed to be his Defence witness. I was supposed to testify about what I testified about today.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And other than Admiral Jokic one year ago, has anyone else contacted you? Not for trial, but as part of an investigation as to what occurred on the 6th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you were contacted on the 5th of December by your commander and told to report on December 6th to Zarkovica, isn't that correct, and you did so?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He did not say that I was supposed to show up at Zarkovica. He gave me a task that clearly spelled out what I was supposed to do. It wasn't a question of showing up or reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you were told that there was a battle plan and that the guns would be ready; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told that I was supposed to give fire support when the feature of Srdj was being taken, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, did anyone tell you that negotiations were being finalised for a cease-fire on the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not aware of that. I did not know about that. As for the cease-fires, there were quite a few of them, and every one of them was observed by me, and of course by the unit that I was subordinated to.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did anyone tell you that Admiral Jokic was negotiating with ministers of the Croatian government, basically the top level of the Croatian government, and that a cease-fire would probably occur at 12.00 noon on December 6th, 1991? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Admiral Jokic, by the very nature of his job, had representatives -- had contacts with the representatives of the local authorities, and further on, the government of Croatia. Now, whether it was specifically on that day, and when the cease-fire was supposed to enter into force, I don't know exactly. I just know that these talks were always conducted in relation to the cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But you were not aware that a cease-fire was planned to occur on the following day, on December 6th, the same day that the JNA was attacking Mount Srdj?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, one last document I'd like to show you. It is D65. Sir, this document is to the command of the 9th VPS, dated December 7th, 1991, at 1.00; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my colleague phrased the question properly, but it was not interpreted into B/C/S properly. So could my colleague please put the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, this is a letter to the command of the 9th VPS at 1.00 on December 7th, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It's from the command of the 9th VPS, for General Simunovic of the First Administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, do you see the paragraph? It's in the middle. In English it's on the second page. It says: "Considering that the commander of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade assessed that the enemy had crossed the line of tolerance." Do you see that paragraph on the second page, sir, second page in the English?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I did not hear your question because I focused on reading the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If you see the beginning of the document, it has a 1 and then a 1A and then a 1B, and then another 1B. And then two paragraphs down from that, it says: "Considering that the commander of the 3rd/472nd MBTR, Motorised Brigade, assessed that the enemy had crossed the line of tolerance." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you read that paragraph, sir? It's a long paragraph. Could you read it, please.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The action on Srdj -- oh, I see. Now that you've told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, have you read the paragraph?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you agree with me that it describes firing upon the JNA troops during the morning? Have you --

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And do you agree, sir, that nowhere in that paragraph does it say that there was any fire from the Old Town? Isn't that correct? Nowhere in that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. And do you agree --

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Until the attack starts -- before the attack started at 6.00 a.m., our forces were fired at from the Old Town of Dubrovnik. So it's not true that there is no reference to that here. There is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It says: "Heavy fire was opened on our forces from 82 millimetres from the city of Dubrovnik, which lasted until 1430 hours."

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the town of Dubrovnik, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The city. But it doesn't --

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: There's a difference between the city of Dubrovnik and the Old Town of Dubrovnik. The city of Dubrovnik is a municipality that takes several areas. Nowhere in this document does it say from the Old Town, sir; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The town or city of Dubrovnik is a broader notion, including the narrower notion of the Old Town of Dubrovnik. So one does not exclude the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But nowhere in this document does it say there was any outgoing fire from the Old Town, specifically indicate the Old Town; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not said very precisely. It says from the city of Dubrovnik. So I cannot say. It says from the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But nowhere in the document does it say "the Old Town," that there was outgoing fire from the Old Town; isn't that correct, sir? I'm not looking to your opinions, your views. I'm looking at this document. Nowhere in the document does it list -- does it say "the Old Town." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The position from where it was coming is not spelled out specifically anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, nowhere in the document does it say "the Old Town," is that correct, that there was outgoing fire from the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, if I were to say that, I would be contesting this document. I mean, I don't agree with what is being said. It is not precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... your opinion. I'm not asking you for your observations. I'm asking --

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What are you asking me about if you're not asking me for my opinion?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm asking not for your observations or what you saw. I'm asking you about this document. Nowhere in this document does it say that there was outgoing fire from the Old Town. It's a simple question. It's either yes or it's no. Look at the document. Nowhere in there does it say there was outgoing fire from the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of that question -- I mean, you're asking me to give an unequivocal answer to an illogical question. Fire was opened from the town of Dubrovnik or the city of Dubrovnik. I cannot simply answer yes or no. The question is not put properly. I cannot give you an answer. Please don't insist.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, if your counsel wants to object, he can object and the Court can decide on that matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber will intervene, though. If you're merely asking the witness: Are the words "Old Town" there, you don't need an answer. They're not there. If he says the city of Dubrovnik or the town of Dubrovnik includes the Old Town, so he is not willing to say this document isn't referring to the Old Town. It can't be taken further than that, can it, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. He can say that the Old Town is not referred to in that context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In so many words. But it may be included in the reference to the city of Dubrovnik. That's what he said some time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, let's go to the sentence halfway down: "From 7.45 to 8.30 hours, the ladder from 9.00, 10.00 to 11.15 hours, the commander of the 3rd of the 5th PMTBR fired on MB," which is mortar battery positions, "on the noticed Zenga groups in the regions." And they are Lazaret [phoen], Hotel Neptun, Nuncijat, Sustjepan, Hotel Petka, Babin Kuk, Libertas. That is all targets, and it says: "Outside of the Old Town." Is that correct, they're all targets outside of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could the witness be provided with document D62 first, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Pepic, would you please take a look at the document first and tell us: Who issued the document and what type of document it is.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a report of the command of the 9th VPS, sent to the command of the 2nd Operational Group. So it's a regular combat report, dated the 6th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Take a look now, please, at who compiled the document and you'll find that on page 2.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Chief of Staff, warship Captain Milan Zec.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you now take a look at it and tell us whether it is the same Captain Zec who was at Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Who was at Zarkovica on the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I've just stated.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please make pauses between question and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... during cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the last ten minutes of the cross-examination by my learned colleague, we have had direct reference to what I have just shown the witness, so would you please allow me to go ahead. As my colleague insists, everything is contained in the document. So I think there is every reason to present this document to the witness. Paragraph 1, and I can read it out if you would like me to do so. Precisely contains the answers to the questions just raised by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In my note, it was D65 that was shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, he was shown D65. Absolutely correct. Now, D62 is before the witness now, and this has a direct bearing on what my learned colleague Mr. Weiner asked related to D65. It clarifies the point and question raised by my learned friend. And if you will allow me to ask a question about the Old Town and firing from the Old Town in the reports of the 9th VPS, we'll be able to clear that up. There were two reports by the 9th VPS. One report was D65 and the second one is the regular combat report bearing the number D62. They relate to the same events, the same circumstances, but the explanations lie in this particular document, D62. I can read it out if you so desire, and then you will see the relevance of what I'm saying, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I have the D62 now, and it's not a report to the First Administration for General Simunovic. It's a report to the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. It is a regular combat report of the 9th VPS to the 2nd Operational Group for the day, the 6th of December, which sets out the data which coincide with what this witness testified about. And I'd like to ask the Court's permission for me to show the document to the witness. And I'm referring to the last sentence of paragraph 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think this is an issue which can be seen to properly arise from the cross-examination, especially that last part. If it's confined to that last sentence at paragraph 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Just the last sentence, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pepic, in the document before you, which is document D62, would you please read out what it says under number 1 about the enemy. Have you read that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Does it say there in that regular combat report of the 9th VPS information about the operations of the enemy from the region of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please read out what it says. The last sentence, please.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was wondering whether to. It says the enemy kept changing the positions of the mortar so that fire was occasionally opened from the Stradun region as well as from the old city port.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pepic, what the command of the 9th VPS is informing the 2nd Operational Group about and the military naval district about, does it correspond to what you yourself saw and what you testified about before this Honourable Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does, completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Totally leading question. This isn't cross-examination [sic].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You understand that, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There's no need for that sort of objection, because you ought to be able to put your questions properly on such a matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Yes. There's no need for me to dwell on this document any longer. It speaks for itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pepic, you said, you told us, that you talked to Admiral Jokic in preparation for his defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And you told Admiral Jokic everything you told us here in Court today?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object at this time. It's totally outside the relevance of our case that we're dealing with here. There might be attorney/client privilege between what he said to Admiral Jokic, what he said to Admiral Jokic's investigators, and it's not relevant to this matter. That's why I got right off it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, the last part is obvious. There's no relevance in that, Mr. Petrovic, to our case, whatever he may have said to Admiral Jokic. If you would leave that topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you, Mr. Pepic, the 107th OAG, your superior command, did you inform them about everything you had observed that day in Zarkovica on the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is to say my first command for opening fire came at 8.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you concentrate on my question, please. Let me repeat: Did you inform your superior command about the events at Zarkovica, that is to say, the command of the 107th OAG?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About my firing positions, yes, I did, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did the command of the 107th OAG report its -- to its superior command on what you had reported to them about?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume they did. They certainly did, because we see that from the events that followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He's speculating now. I assume -- he said I assume he did and then he said: Certainly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is speculative. You can ask whether he knows. I think we clearly have the answer to that. You really can't take it further than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever, on any subject, report or inform the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: My colleague asked you about the fire that was opened between six to ten on the Old Town on that day, the 6th, with respect to the length of it, the 6th of December. Was fire really opened between six and ten on the positions of the JNA and the region you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would appear that there was fire all the time. It didn't last that long.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, not clear whether time, 6.00 to 10.00 a.m. or the number of hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did anybody ever, from the 9th VPS, call you to make a statement or clarify the events of the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us briefly once again how you distinguish between the flash of a mortar explosion from the flash caused from the mouth of a barrel.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The flash caused from the mouth of a barrel comes immediately after the shell leaves the barrel, and just as a flash of light expands, the sound of the shell falling is much weaker. So you only see a flash without fragmentation and without smoke. The flash of a mortar, you hear the fragmentation and dispersion of construction material and so on, and you see fire and smoke to follow. And it's an enormous difference, a huge difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How much practice do you yourself have in distinguishing between the firing and detonation, explosion?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am the -- I was the commander of a battery for seven years, six years, in actual fact, the commander of a platoon and a battery, and each year we would have at least two shooting sessions with an active army, and we had training and exercise with my protection part, which includes an 82-millimetre battery. And during that shooting and firing that I took part in myself, or rather that I was in command of and observed, there is no calibre from which I did not shoot myself. So I know absolutely everything there is to know in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think it's time for a break. I have another five or ten minutes of re-examination of this witness. So I suggest, if you approve, of course, that we take a break, our second break for the day now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at a quarter to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Just a few short questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pepic, you testified over the past two days to the effect that it was your assignment on the 6th of December to lend support to Captain Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You were supposed to give Captain Kovacevic artillery support with your battery's 130-millimetre cannons?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You were supposed to be re-subordinated to Captain Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I did.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please slow down and make pauses between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You got your assignment from your commander; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And the assignment was to open fire pursuant to orders from the commander of the 3rd Battalion; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, right. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Was there any initiative on your part in any of this?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Would you now take a look at the document D65, please. Mr. Pepic, you saw the document a moment ago when it was shown to you by my learned friend; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Towards the end of the first page of that document, on the B/C/S version, it says the following: That the commander of that unit of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade made the decision to attack Srdj and eliminate the danger but that nobody approved that operation. Now, is what it says in this report, does it coincide with what you know about the operation on Srdj? Is it the same thing?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, quite obviously it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You told us yesterday --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You told us yesterday in your evidence that you were ordered by Captain Kovacevic to fire, I think you said on the first occasion at about 0800 hours. Mortars had been identified, firing in the vicinity of the Libertas Hotel and tennis courts there. You said you gave the order to your battery. That means you used your radio to communicate with your battery commander, is that right, or your deputy commander down there?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: When you gave that order, there was no firing?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Was it the role of the deputy commander to get authority to fire from a superior command?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not have to receive authority. I was subordinate to Captain Kovacevic. However, the commander of the artillery battalion used his right to prevent and did prevent the opening of fire. And that was Lieutenant Colonel Stamenov.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And where was he located?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was located near the firing position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Down at Cilipi, in the area of Cilipi?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. My battery was between two paths, and he was in the airport building itself. So as the crow flies, about 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So it was the battery commander who refused permission to fire each time you gave an order to fire; is that it?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It wasn't the commander of the battery; it was the commander of the artillery battalion. That was a higher rank. I was battery commander, he was commander of the division or artillery battalion, and he stopped the firing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you able to say how many times you gave an order to fire that day?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I issued my order at 0800 hours, and I repeated the order at least twice. The next came at around 9.00, and by 9.30 there was one more. I know about that for certain. That's what I'm sure about. And I was in radio communication with the deputy commander, and I was explaining the situation to him. So I was explaining our losses to him. May I be allowed to continue? And I clearly observed the target and that I said that I needed only two shells for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And each time the target was this mortar position near the Libertas Hotel; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Was it only those three times that you gave an order for firing that day?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that it was three times for certain. The rest was to persuade the superior command to grant me permission, because had that permission been granted for the firing, I can say with certainty that none of the rest of it would ever have happened. That is to say, there wouldn't have been the bombing of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Were you ever told the reason of your battalion commander for not authorising the firing?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In an informal information, I learnt that it wasn't his order; it was an order from the command of the 9th Military Naval Sector, in fact, and they were abreast of the situation throughout. The reason was that the shell might have made an error and fallen into the Old Town itself by mistake, and that could not have happened in any event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is it the case that the battalion commander was in contact with the command of the 9th Military Naval Sector?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So whenever you requested permission to fire, he contacted the 9th Military Naval Sector; is that it?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely so, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: How did he do that? Did he have radio or telephone, or what was his communication?

utterances.speaker: VLADO PEPIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had at least two types of communication: A telephone communication, cable, and radio communication. Now, in this particular case, as it was the command posts which had been taken control of for some time, it was telephone communication and, in principle, you first resort to telephone communication, and only afterwards do you resort to radio communication or a human being in the form of a courier to convey your messages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to thank you for your attendance and your assistance. You'll be pleased to know that that's the end of your evidence and you are now free to return to your duties. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank you too, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Next witness, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, Your Honour. The Defence would like to call our next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Would you please read the affirmation that is on the card.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, can you please state your full name to the Court.

utterances.speaker: PETRE HANDZIJEV
utterances.text: My name is Petre Handzijev.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us your date of birth and place of birth?

utterances.speaker: PETRE HANDZIJEV
utterances.text: I was born on the 10th of March, 1943, in the village of Rakite, in the Republic of Greece. The Greeks refer to the village as Olimpias.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What's your nationally?

utterances.speaker: PETRE HANDZIJEV
utterances.text: I am an Aegean Macedonian by ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us your education background?

utterances.speaker: PETRE HANDZIJEV
utterances.text: I completed my secondary education in Skopje, the naval military academy at Split. Then a specialised course following the completion of military academy, and then further specialised courses for anti-submarine fighting in the late 1980s.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Were you an active member of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: PETRE HANDZIJEV
utterances.text: I was an active member of the JNA from 1966 to 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What's your status at present?

utterances.speaker: PETRE HANDZIJEV
utterances.text: I am -- I have retired.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What was your rank at the time you retired?

utterances.speaker: PETRE HANDZIJEV
utterances.text: Warship captain.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: This is a navy rank. Can you please tell us in terms of infantry ranks, what would that be, roughly speaking?

utterances.speaker: PETRE HANDZIJEV
utterances.text: Colonel, the rank of colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the course of your career in the JNA, which garrisons did you serve in?

utterances.speaker: PETRE HANDZIJEV
utterances.text: Between 1966 and 1978, I served at the gunship artillery battalion at Lora, in Split, and this was a special unit which was providing security for the Marsala Tita barracks. Correction, for Marsal Tito personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Where did you go to serve after 1978?

utterances.speaker: PETRE HANDZIJEV
utterances.text: After 1978, I got a transfer to the 9th Military Naval Sector in Boka Kotorska.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In the 9th Military Naval Sector, in Boka, is that where you stayed until your retirement?

utterances.speaker: PETRE HANDZIJEV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us which positions you held for most of your service with the 9th VPS.

utterances.speaker: PETRE HANDZIJEV
utterances.text: I was an administrator in the operations and teaching department, and I spent my whole time there in that same department.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Who does that department belong to? Who or to which command does that department belong to?

utterances.speaker: PETRE HANDZIJEV
utterances.text: It's part of the 9th VPS command.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Where was the command post of the 9th VPS?

utterances.speaker: PETRE HANDZIJEV
utterances.text: It was at the headquarters, at the command building, on the second floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And what is the location?

utterances.speaker: PETRE HANDZIJEV
utterances.text: Kumbor.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In 1991, which position did you hold?

utterances.speaker: PETRE HANDZIJEV
utterances.text: 1991, my position was that of the chief of the operations centre of the peacetime command. I was also a member of a team for professional duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: This duty, was it carried out at the operations centre of the command of the 9th VPS at Kumbor?

utterances.speaker: PETRE HANDZIJEV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What do we find in the operational centre of the 9th VPS command at Kumbor? What was there? What did the operational centre include?

utterances.speaker: PETRE HANDZIJEV
utterances.text: There's an operations room. There's another room, the communications department. The encryption officer. It has an observation station, a coastal observation station, monitoring the situation, and an air monitoring unit or department.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us which officers were on duty at the operational centre.
